rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A **perfect black body** absorbs all incident radiation and, by Kirchhoff's law, emits the maximum possible at every wavelength; it is realised practically as a **cavity with a tiny hole**. Its spectrum is continuous, peaking at $\lambda_{max} = 2.9\times10^{-3}/T$ (**Wien's displacement law**) — hotter bodies glow at shorter wavelengths, from dull red to white-hot, and the Sun's 5800 K peak sits in the visible.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - λ_max T = 2.9×10⁻³ m·K (Wien) - E_total = σT⁴ (Stefan–Boltzmann) - Planck: E = hν

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **A 'black body' can glow white** — 'black' means perfect absorption, not appearance.  ·  **Wien's law:** hotter → peak shifts to shorter wavelength (λ_maxT = const).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "A perfect black body absorbs all radiation incident on it and is the best possible emitter."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Sun*** — T ≈ 5800 K peaks at ~500 nm: exactly where our eyes see best.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: No verified PYQ; NEB-style practice (definition 3m, Wien's law 2–3m).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Colour of Heat Heat a horseshoe and it glows dull red, then orange, then white. That colour sequence is black-body radiation — the universal spectrum that every hot object approaches, the spectrum that forced Planck to invent the quantum and so started modern physics.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 What is a black body? A **perfect black body** absorbs all incident radiation ($a = 1$) regardless of wavelength or direction. By Kirchhoff's law it is also the best possible emitter at every wavelength.…

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A star's radiation peaks at 290 nm. Find its surface temperature.** — T = 2.9×10⁻³/290×10⁻⁹ = 10⁴ K — a hot blue-white star.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Expect the cavity construction and Wien's law; Stefan's law is a separate topic.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The ultraviolet catastrophe and Planck's fix** — black-body radiation is where quantum physics was born.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Black body: a = 1; realised by a cavity with a small hole.  ·  λ_max T = 2.9×10⁻³ m·K; spectrum continuous, area ∝ T⁴.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The cosmic microwave background (2.7 K) is the most precise black-body spectrum ever measured.
